items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: This research explores the capability of large language models to modify their own internal parameters through a self-referential rewriting process. It investigates whether models can autonomously update their knowledge or logic by directly altering the weights that define their behavior.
items.why_it_matters: If models can reliably rewrite their own weights, it could lead to autonomous self-improvement and more efficient knowledge updates without full retraining. This represents a shift from static inference to dynamic, self-evolving neural architectures.

items.title: CodePilot Tutorial: Multi-Model AI Agent Desktop App with a Free Local Model (Ollama, Step by Step)
items.summary: CodePilot is a desktop-based AI agent application that can read, write, and execute terminal commands within a local project folder after user approval. It supports multiple AI providers, including local models via Ollama, allowing for private development workflows without mandatory API keys.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a bridge between LLMs and local file systems, enabling automated coding tasks while maintaining a 'human-in-the-loop' security model for command execution. The support for local models via Ollama addresses privacy concerns for developers working on sensitive codebases.

items.title: Google is pushing OEMs against GrapheneOS and bootloader unlocking
items.summary: GrapheneOS has reported that Google is allegedly pressuring original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) to restrict bootloader unlocking, which would prevent users from installing privacy-focused alternative operating systems.
items.why_it_matters: Bootloader unlocking is the foundational requirement for hardware ownership and custom ROM development; restricting it centralizes control over mobile security and privacy within the official vendor ecosystem.

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.summary: This article highlights a growing security threat where attackers steal or manipulate authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to systems. It emphasizes the shift from traditional password theft to more sophisticated token-based exploitation.
items.why_it_matters: As multi-factor authentication becomes standard, attackers are bypassing it entirely by hijacking active session tokens. This represents a critical shift in the threat landscape for any developer managing user sessions or API keys.
